title: Smallest Missing Genetic Value in Each Subtree
summary: Given a family tree with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where each node has a unique genetic value in the range [1, 100000], find the smallest genetic value missing in the subtree rooted at each node.
statement: Given a family tree with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where each node has a unique genetic value in the range [1, 100000], find the smallest genetic value missing in the subtree rooted at each node. Return an array where each element corresponds to the root node and its missing genetic value.
constraints: parents and nums have equal length 2 through 100000; parents describes a tree rooted at zero.
Genetic values are distinct integers from 1 through 100000.
For every node, return the smallest positive value absent from its subtree.
reference_solution:
def smallest_missing_genetic_values(parents,nums):
    n=len(nums);answer=[1]*n
    if 1 not in nums:return answer
    children=[[] for _ in range(n)]
    for node in range(1,n):children[parents[node]].append(node)
    visited=[False]*n;present=set();missing=1
    def add(root):
        stack=[root]
        while stack:
            node=stack.pop()
            if visited[node]:continue
            visited[node]=True;present.add(nums[node]);stack.extend(children[node])
    node=nums.index(1)
    while node!=-1:
        add(node)
        while missing in present:missing+=1
        answer[node]=missing;node=parents[node]
    return answer

hints: Any subtree without value one immediately has answer one, so only one ancestor chain needs work.
Start at the node containing one and walk to the root, incrementally adding each newly included subtree to one shared set.
DFS each unvisited ancestor subtree; advance missing while present; record it; move to parent.
Off-chain subtrees lack one. Along the chain, visited nodes only grow and each tree node is added once, so every recorded set is exactly that ancestor’s subtree.
